title: Sunni and Shia Islam — Tradition Overview (Edition 1)
description: Sunnis, the majority, emphasize community consensus and the Prophet's example, while Shia Muslims revere Ali and the Imams as rightful successors. Both affirm the Quran, the Prophet, and the Five Pillars. This overview edition presents Sunni and Shia Islam within the world's religious landscape, factually and without favor.

spec.overview: Sunnis, the majority, emphasize community consensus and the Prophet's example, while Shia Muslims revere Ali and the Imams as rightful successors. Both affirm the Quran, the Prophet, and the Five Pillars.
core_beliefs: Succession through consensus versus designated Imams
practices: Largely shared worship with some differences
holidays: Shared Eids; Ashura prominent in Shia observance
spec.adherents: Sunnis form the large majority of Muslims worldwide.

example.fact: Iran, Iraq, Bahrain, and Azerbaijan have Shia-majority populations.

spec.study_note: Core facts verified from public sources; adherent figures are estimates from the Pew Research Center.
